exposure: fetal diagnosis of diencephalic-mesencephalic junction dysplasia (DMJD)
fetal MRI phenotypes (Type A, Type B, Type C)
genetic etiologies (L1CAM mutations, biallelic VRK1 variants)
outcome: postnatal brain MRI confirmation of diagnosis
cohort: The study included 33 pregnancies with fetal MRI findings of diencephalic-mesencephalic junction dysplasia (DMJD) at 24 (18-37) weeks gestational age.
finding: The study identified three distinct fetal MRI phenotypic forms of DMJD (Types A-C) and found that next-generation sequencing can provide an underlying molecular diagnosis in some patients, with all surviving infants experiencing developmental delay and additional neurological sequelae.
